_region_note: Five distinct regions cover eight states on purpose — Qing China and Tokugawa Japan share East Asia, Benin/Ashanti/Dahomey share West Africa. See the module docstring: that overlap is the point of the unit, not a shortcut.
intro: Eight states from Day 1. Match each one to the region it actually sat in, about 1750 — not the region its size might suggest.

left.label: Ottoman Empire
hints: This empire was big enough to reach onto three continents.
Pick the region that names three parts of the world at once.

left.label: Mughal Empire
hints: Aurangzeb ruled this empire, from India.
It's the subcontinent: the big wedge of land south of the Himalayas.

left.label: Qing China
hints: This is China's ruling dynasty in 1750. Which region is China part of?
China shares its region with one other state on this list, a group of islands just to the east.

left.label: Tokugawa Japan
hints: Japan is a group of islands. Which big mainland neighbor sits closest to it?
Japan and China sit in the same region.

left.label: Russian Empire
hints: This empire stretched from Europe all the way east to the Pacific.
Think far north, on two continents at once.

left.label: Benin
hints: Benin traded pepper, ivory and cloth with Europeans who arrived by sea.
Three states on this list share one region, on Africa's Atlantic coast.

left.label: Ashanti
hints: Ashanti grew rich on gold. Its land is part of the country of Ghana today.
It sits on the same coast as Benin and Dahomey.

left.label: Dahomey
hints: Dahomey was a kingdom on Africa's Atlantic coast that traded with Europeans who came by ship.
It shares a region with Benin and Ashanti.

right.label: Southeastern Europe, southwest Asia, and North Africa

rationale.a: The Ottoman Empire ruled from southeastern Europe through southwest Asia into North Africa — the one empire on this list that reached across three continents.
rationale.b: The Mughal Empire ruled most of the Indian subcontinent — South Asia.
rationale.c: Qing China was the largest and richest state in the world by almost any measure you can name, sitting in East Asia.
rationale.d: Tokugawa Japan sat east of China and had deliberately shut itself off from nearly all foreign contact — same region as Qing China, East Asia, a very different relationship with the rest of the world.
rationale.e: The Russian Empire was pushing east across Asia in 1750 — a land empire spanning northern Europe and northern Asia.
rationale.f: Benin was one of the wealthy, well-organized kingdoms on the West African coast, trading pepper, ivory and cloth with Europeans who arrived by sea.
rationale.g: Ashanti was one of the wealthy, well-organized kingdoms on the West African coast, and it grew rich on the gold traded with Europeans who arrived by sea.
rationale.h: Dahomey was one of the wealthy, well-organized kingdoms on the West African coast, trading with Europeans who arrived by sea, above all in captured people.
